teams.heading: Fiji Rugby partners with Coca-Cola to launch commemorative sevens cans
teams.body: Fiji Rugby has partnered with Coca-Cola Europacific Partners to launch limited-edition collectable cans and bottles celebrating the Fiji Airways Men’s 7s team. Unveiled at Albert Park in Suva, the commemorative packs feature eight iconic moments from the 2025 Hong Kong and Singapore tournaments. Fiji Rugby Commercial Director Tevita Tuiloa welcomed the campaign, stating, "This is more than the launch of a new product." The initiative aims to connect the country's passion for the sport with community inspiration.

lead.why: It is the main new development of the day, highlighting a major commercial partnership and commemorative campaign for the national sevens side.

teams.heading: England hooker Jamie Blamire starts for Leicester Tigers in Slater Cup return
teams.body: England hooker Jamie Blamire will return to the Leicester Tigers starting line-up for Friday’s Slater Cup clash with Gloucester at Welford Road. Blamire is one of five changes made by coach Geoff Parling after recovering from injury to join fellow internationals Joe Heyes and Freddie Steward in the XV. Captain Jack van Poortvliet also starts, though Adam Radwan is rotated to the replacements. For the visitors, England centre Will Joseph retains his midfield spot in a Gloucester side currently sitting top of the table.

teams.heading: Owen Doyle condemns Michael Hooper and Sir Steve Hansen regarding Piardi
teams.body: Former IRFU director of referees Owen Doyle has labelled recent comments from Michael Hooper and Sir Steve Hansen as “totally out of order.” The pair had suggested that World Rugby should prevent Italian official Andrea Piardi from refereeing future Australia matches, citing concerns over player and referee welfare. Doyle challenged this stance, arguing that the criticism levelled at Piardi following the Wallabies' win over the Springboks was misdirected, particularly as the referee contended with significant technical failures regarding TMO communications.

teams.heading: Italy assess performance metrics as squad prepares for South Africa fixture
teams.body: As Italy prepares for their upcoming Nations Championship encounter, the side looks to address their recent scoring form. Across their last 11 matches, the Azzurri have recorded 190 points, averaging 17.3 points per game, while conceding 318 points at an average of 28.9. The team aims to replicate their attacking output from their most successful result in this window, where they secured a 34-19 home victory against Chile in November 2025.

teams.heading: Brain injury legal action faces ongoing threat of collapse this month
teams.body: The high-profile legal action regarding brain injuries in rugby remains in a precarious position as claimants continue to face a significant £2.8m legal bill. While recent court battles have prevented the cases from being thrown out, the financial burden remains the primary obstacle to the proceedings continuing. With the deadline to settle these mounting legal fees approaching this month, the future of the litigation against governing bodies remains uncertain for all parties involved, including those within the Scottish game.

teams.heading: Wales back Max Llewellyn returns to Gloucester bench for Slater Cup
teams.body: Welsh international Max Llewellyn has been named among the replacements for Gloucester ahead of Friday night's Slater Cup clash against Leicester Tigers. The midfielder’s return to the matchday squad provides a boost for the visitors as they look to maintain their unbeaten start to the season. Gloucester currently sit at the top of the log and seek a third consecutive victory at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, facing a Leicester side bolstered by the return of several high-profile internationals.

teams.heading: Argentina overpower Wales with dominant five-try display in Nations Championship
teams.body: Argentina showcased their attacking potential in the Nations Championship by securing a 35-21 victory over Wales. Despite a defeat to Scotland in the tournament opener, the Pumas recovered to brush aside the Welsh challenge in San Juan. The result highlighted a clinical side that scored five tries, effectively halting a mini-revival from the visitors. The win offers a boost to the squad as they continue their campaign, having also navigated a testing loss to England during the competition.

teams.heading: Isaac Henry replaces Hunter Paisami as Wallabies face All Blacks away
teams.body: Les Kiss has named a settled starting side for the Bledisloe Cup opener at Eden Park, with Isaac Henry called up to start at outside centre. Henry’s inclusion is the only change to the XV that defeated South Africa in Perth, as Len Ikitau shifts to inside centre to cover for the suspended Hunter Paisami. Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii has been retained on the wing to maintain back-three consistency. "Keeping consistency in the starting side gives us a solid foundation," noted Kiss.

teams.heading: Japan Sakura 7s Reclaim Gold at the 20th Asian Games Tournament
teams.body: Japan’s women secured a notable victory at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, defeating defending champions China 10-5 in a tightly contested final. The result marks the first time the Sakura 7s have reclaimed the gold medal since their success two Games ago. While the Japanese men’s side settled for bronze after a 17-5 win over Korea, the women’s triumph highlighted a competitive weekend of sevens, with the hosts overcoming a resilient Chinese team to secure the top podium spot.

teams.heading: Damian McKenzie starts at flyhalf as Richie Mo'unga misses Bledisloe tests
teams.body: Damian McKenzie will shift from fullback to flyhalf for Saturday’s opening Bledisloe Cup clash at Eden Park after Richie Mo'unga was ruled out of the entire series. Mo'unga sustained a calf tear during training on Tuesday, forcing a late reshuffle of the backline. Beauden Barrett will slot in at fullback for his first start of the year. Dave Rennie described the injury as "disappointing for the group" but noted that his playmakers remain highly interchangeable in the team’s current structure.

teams.heading: Eben Etzebeth returns as Sharks promote three Springboks for Stormers clash
teams.body: Eben Etzebeth has been named in the Sharks starting XV for Saturday’s United Rugby Championship derby against the Stormers in Cape Town. The lock is joined by fellow Springboks Ox Nché and Ethan Hooker in being promoted to the run-on side following their recent international duty. Head coach JP Pietersen has opted for a 6-2 split on the bench for the fixture, as the Durban-based outfit looks to maintain their unbeaten start to the new campaign.
